title: kv-pool-allocator-eviction-proposal
content:
Purpose and scope:

This working draft describes the KV (key-value) cache architecture we want to adopt in the serving runtime. Focus areas: physical layout in GPU memory, allocator / memory pools, fragmentation mitigation, eviction policies, accounting, and interactions with the scheduler and model kernels. This doc is intentionally pragmatic: contains concrete data structures, heuristics we plan to try, and a short experiment plan.

Context and goals:
- Primary goal: keep latency predictable for autoregressive workloads while minimizing GPU memory usage and fragmentation.
- Secondary goals: multi-model sharing on the same GPU, per-tenant isolation limits, and graceful degradation when memory pressure is high (fallback to recompute or remote store).
- Constraints: frequent small writes (per token per layer KV append), long-lived KV entries (chat sessions), variable KV sizes (different models, quantizations, sequence lengths).

High-level design summary:
1) Page-based slab allocator pinned to GPU memory with three pool classes: tiny, small, and large.
2) KV entries stored as contiguous pages; each logical entry has a header (meta) stored alongside the data to speed lookup and compaction.
3) Eviction: hybrid policy = LRU-approximation (CLOCK) with probationARY sampling + size-aware cost metric; prefer evicting large cold entries that free contiguous pages to reduce fragmentation.
4) Compaction: background GPU-side copy/migrate when free pages become scattered above threshold; avoid blocking inference by per-shard quiescence.
5) Allocation accounting and quotas per model + per-customer to preserve isolation.
6) Instrumentation: per-allocation timestamps, last-access counters, fragmentation metrics (free-run-length histograms), and eviction logs.

Memory layout and metadata:
- Page size: baseline 64KB (configurable). Rationale: small enough to reduce wasted space for small KV tensors (typical layer KV chunk ~8–128KB depending on dtype), but large enough to keep page table small and reduce syscall/driver overhead.
- Slab buckets: tiny (1 page), small (2–8 pages contiguous), large (>8 pages contiguous). Each slab tracks a free-run-length map and owner id.
- Logical KV entry: header fields stored in a separate small GPU resident metadata array mapped into CPU addressable pinned memory for fast reads by control-plane threads:
  - key_id (64-bit) -- combination of model_namespace, session_id, layer_index, head_group
  - size_bytes (32-bit)
  - pages_start_idx (32-bit)
  - pages_len (16-bit)
  - last_access_epoch (32-bit)
  - flags (8-bit): hot, pinned, in_migrate, eviction_locked
- Metadata is compact and aligned to 64 bytes; metadata array stored in a separate allocation with its own allocator to avoid interleaving with payload fragmentation.

Allocator design and pools:
- Use a global GPU-resident page bitmap + per-stream free lists to reduce contention. Pages are addressed by page index; an allocation returns a contiguous page range when possible.
- Pools:
  * Tiny pool: for allocations <= 1 page. Use freelist of single pages that are cache-coalesced (we try to keep these small pages together in the same page runs).
  * Small pool: 2–8 pages. Maintain segregated lists by length to speed exact-fit allocation.
  * Large pool: >8 pages. Maintain a buddy-like tree to find large contiguous extents; accept splitting into smaller chunks when necessary.
- Allocation strategy: first try same-owner exact or near-exact fit (locality), then global exact fit in same slab, then global best-fit with minimal fragmentation estimate. If only fragmented space available, may trigger background compaction or allow allocation to fall back to remote store or CPU memory (see fallback).
- Per-owner quotas: each model (and tenant where applicable) has soft and hard GPU byte quotas. Soft limit triggers aggressive eviction and compaction attempts; hard limit rejects new allocations or routes to fallback recompute/remote store.

Fragmentation handling and compaction:
- Measure fragmentation via run-length histograms (RLE) on the free page bitmap per slab. Trigger thresholds: mean_free_run_len < 2 pages OR free_fraction < 15% => consider compaction.
- Compaction approach: migrate live KV entries into new contiguous extents using GPU memcpy kernels (vectorized) and update metadata atomically. Use double-buffering for metadata updates: write new header with in_migrate flag, copy payload, flip pages_start_idx, clear old pages, clear in_migrate.
- Compaction scheduling: background worker per-GPU with low priority; quiesce only the pages being moved (lock per-entry eviction_locked flag) and avoid blocking inference streams by issuing async memcpy on dedicated copy streams. If a migrating entry is read by the inference thread, it can be served from either source (copy is in progress) with read-path checking in_migrate flag.
- Fragmentation-resistant allocation heuristics: prefer allocating from slabs reserved for the owner when possible; avoid splitting large runs unless necessary; when splitting large runs we align on power-of-two multiples of page sizes to reduce small-tail fragmentation.

Eviction policy and heuristics:
- Objectives: free contiguous space quickly, minimize recompute/regeneration cost, and preserve latency SLOs.
- Candidate ranking cost = alpha * recency_score + beta * size_cost + gamma * contiguity_bonus + delta * pin_penalty.
  * recency_score from CLOCK-like circular buffer approximating LRU using last_access_epoch.
  * size_cost favors evicting entries that free many contiguous pages. A normalized size term (size_bytes / average_entry_size).
  * contiguity_bonus adds weight to entries whose eviction creates or extends contiguous runs.
  * pin_penalty prevents evicting pinned or in_migrate entries.
- Two-tier eviction flow:
  1) Fast-path: on small pressure, evict tiny cold entries (<= 1 page) using exact LRU buckets.
  2) Slow-path: when contiguous free runs needed (large allocation), run a sampled scan to find the best candidate per cost metric. If insufficient contiguous space, trigger compaction and re-check.
- Eviction consequences: evicted KV entries are either (a) dropped and recomputed on next request, (b) spilled to remote object store (S3-like) asynchronously, or (c) migrated to CPU paged area for soft-offload. Choice depends on owner policy and SLAs; preference order: recompute (if cheap), spill to remote (if long tail session, cold but large), CPU page if low latency necessary.

Concurrency, correctness, and failure modes:
- Concurrency model: per-entry atomic header updates and CAS-based ownership flips. Read path is optimistic: read metadata, check in_migrate/eviction_locked flags, and read payload. If flags change during read, retry. Writes (inserts/extend) obtain eviction_locked for the entry's header and update pages atomically.
- Crash consistency: metadata persisted to a compact mmaped CPU-visible store on controlled shutdown; for abrupt GPU driver reset, we expect to rebuild from upstream KV source (session replay) — make sure we can snapshot mapping to remote store periodically for long-lived sessions.
- Race scenarios: migrating entry being read concurrently — handled by in_migrate flag; evict/compact conflicts resolved by global eviction_mutex per-slab during candidate replacement (coarse-grained but rare).

Integration with serving runtime and scheduler:
- The scheduler requests allocations when a request will append new tokens to an existing session (we know ahead how many pages predicted). Allocation is a pre-step in the token dispatch pipeline. If allocation fails synchronously and fallback allowed, scheduler either delays token emission (NACK backpressure) or routes request to a model variant that recomputes KV less frequently.
- Instrumentation hooks emitted per allocation/eviction: allocation_time_ms, pages_allocated, pages_freed, compaction_bytes, migration_time_ms. These metrics feed into the console and RL-based optimizer later.

APIs (control-plane):
- kv_alloc(key_id, size_bytes, policy={pin, spill_priority, owner_quota_mode}) -> allocation_handle or error
- kv_get(key_id) -> (payload_ptr, size_bytes) or miss
- kv_append(key_id, delta_payload) -> success/fail (for streaming KV writes)
- kv_evict(key_id) -> async_result (used by admin and compaction to voluntarily free space)
- kv_stats(owner) -> json-like string (but stored as a single string field in this doc)

Performance targets / experimentation plan:
- Targets: P99 token generation latency increase < 2ms attributable to KV operations; compaction overhead backgrounded < 5% GPU time; eviction-induced recompute should impact < 0.5% of requests in steady-state.
- Experiments:
  1) Microbench: measure allocation/free throughput at different page sizes (32KB/64KB/128KB) and access patterns (many tiny sessions vs few long sessions).
  2) Eviction sim: run workload traces from production (sampled) through a simulator implementing the cost metric to tune alpha/beta/gamma.
  3) Fragmentation stress: run continuous churn jobs to force fragmentation and measure compaction cost and effectiveness.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Best default page size given mixed precisions (fp16 vs int8) — experiment seems necessary.
- Should we allow non-contiguous scatter-gather KV entries on read (stores multiple small extents per logical KV) to reduce fragmentation at the cost of read complexity?
- How aggressive should background compaction be for multi-tenant GPUs? Need policy for per-owner compaction fairness.
- Policy semantics for eviction: expose per-model hints (recompute_cost_estimate, spillable, min_hot_ttl). How do SDKs and product teams specify these?
- Integration with GPU memory allocator (cudaMalloc hooks vs custom pool): prototype both and benchmark.

Appendix: simple eviction pseudocode (CLOCK + size heuristics)

function pick_eviction_candidate(required_pages):
  for pass in [fast, slow]:
    if pass == fast:
      candidates = sample_recent_bucket(tiny_entries, 128)
    else:
      candidates = sample_global(1024)
    best = None
    best_score = +inf
    for e in candidates:
      if e.pinned or e.in_migrate: continue
      recency = now_epoch - e.last_access_epoch
      size_factor = e.pages_len / avg_pages
      contig_bonus = estimate_contig_gain_if_evicted(e)
      score = alpha*recency - beta*size_factor - gamma*contig_bonus
      if score < best_score:
        best_score = score
        best = e
    if best and best.pages_len >= required_pages:
      return best
  // if nothing found, trigger compaction and retry once
  trigger_compaction()
  retry sample_global(4096)
  return fallback (spill or reject)
Notes for reviewers:
- This is a sketch. Focus review on: eviction scoring terms, compaction safety (race conditions), and the practicalities of implementing asynchronous GPU memcpy-based migration.
- If we agree on the page/slab approach I will prototype the allocator as a standalone lib that can be tested against traces.

Roadmap (next steps):
- Week 1–2: prototype page-based allocator + metadata store; run microbench allocations. (owner: Maya)
- Week 3–4: implement CLOCK-ish LRU sampler + cost metric; simulate using prod traces. (owner: Diego)
- Week 5–8: implement GPU-side migration and background compactor; integrate with serving runtime routing. (owner: Elliot)
- Ongoing: collect telemetry, iterate on parameters, and add per-model policy surfaces to product.

End of draft.

Notes-to-self / scratch lines:
- Consider using 2x copies of metadata for quick atomic swaps instead of CAS heavy path.
- Slack thread: link above has recent perf traces (look at messages from Nov-Dec).
- Jira-RT-2381 contains the request from infra to expose per-tenant hard limits.
